segment.description: The short (~1.5 mile) riverine Watauga River between Watauga Dam and Wilbur Lake (Wilbur Reservoir) in Carter County - the cold, clear release water closing the Watauga Lake -> Wilbur Lake -> Watauga River tailwater chain.
segment.boundaries: Watauga Dam (USGS 03483950 below-dam gauge; spillway-release station 03483600) downstream ~1.5 miles to the head of Wilbur Reservoir (Wilbur Dam sits ~3 river miles below Watauga Dam at Watauga River Mile 34 per TWRA's Wilbur Tailwater plan). SIBLING TRAP GUARD: this is NOT the celebrated Wilbur tailwater below Wilbur Dam (catalog watauga-river, batch-1 high-confidence record) - none of that record's facts are transferred here.

coldSource.notes: TWRA's Wilbur Tailwater Trout Fishery Management Plan 2022-2027 (cited URL, not fetched per PDF policy; text quoted in batch-1/wave-ledger records) fixes the geometry - Wilbur Dam at WRM 34 impounds a ~72-acre re-regulating pool about 3 miles below Watauga Dam - and documents turbine venting of Watauga Dam discharges so the chain's releases meet TVA's 6.0 mg/L DO target, i.e. deep (bottom) releases. Direct temperature evidence for water transiting this dam-to-dam chain: USGS-03483980 'WATAUGA RIVER AT WILBUR DAM, TN (TAILWATER)' - the discharge at the far (downstream) end of Wilbur Reservoir - measured 8.0 C (6/22/1976), 8.0 C (7/19/1976), 9.5 C (7/20/1976), 10.0 C (8/16/1976), 12.0-13.0 C in September, and 6.0-11.0 C across winter 1975-76 (WQP Result search below). Those samples sit below the 72-acre pool, so the release water is at or colder than that when it enters this reach; ~1,550 ft elevation per USGS 03484000 datum used for the chain in batch-1. Dam-release flow in this reach follows TVA generation schedules; minimum-flow/intermittency was not assessed in this pass.

holdover.detail: No fishery survey or holdover study specific to this 1.5-mile reach was found; TWRA's Wilbur plan documents holdover/survival for the tailwater BELOW Wilbur Dam (a different catalog entry), and the 2017-2027 statewide plan counts Wilbur Reservoir among the nine reservoirs with maintained trout fisheries. For the reach itself: unknown.

wildPopulation.detail: No natural-reproduction data specific to the reach. Trout stocked at both ends of the chain (Watauga Lake; Wilbur Reservoir Mar-Jul; Wilbur tailwater below) necessarily transit this water, but no in-reach survey documents reproduction.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The release water transiting this Watauga-Dam-to-Wilbur chain measured 8.0-9.5 C in June-July 1976 and never exceeded 13 C in any season at the chain's discharge gauge (USGS-03483980) - bottom-draw dam water far below any summer trout stress threshold, year-round.
